title: Spliterator characteristics: ORDERED, SIZED, SORTED, DISTINCT and stream optimizations
keyPoints: Spliterator characteristics are bit flags that describe properties of the data source: ORDERED, SIZED, SORTED, DISTINCT, NONNULL, IMMUTABLE, CONCURRENT, SUBSIZED.
SIZED means the exact element count is known upfront, enabling the stream to pre-allocate arrays for toArray() without resizing.
SORTED means elements are already sorted, so a sorted() operation in the stream is a no-op.
DISTINCT means no duplicates exist, so a distinct() operation in the stream is a no-op.
ORDERED means elements have a defined encounter order, which affects forEachOrdered() in parallel streams.
Different collections report different characteristics: ArrayList is ORDERED + SIZED, HashSet is DISTINCT + SIZED, TreeSet is ORDERED + SORTED + DISTINCT + SIZED.
Stream operations can add or remove characteristics: filter() removes SIZED, sorted() adds SORTED, distinct() adds DISTINCT.

s1_definition.oneliner: Spliterator characteristics are bit flags that describe data source properties like ordering, sizing, and uniqueness, enabling the stream pipeline to skip redundant operations and pre-allocate storage.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **ORDERED** (0x10) – elements have a defined encounter order; List and LinkedHashSet report this; HashSet and HashMap do not
- **DISTINCT** (0x01) – all elements are unique; Set implementations report this; the stream can skip distinct()
- **SORTED** (0x04) – elements are sorted in natural or comparator order; TreeSet and TreeMap report this; the stream can skip sorted()
- **SIZED** (0x40) – exact element count is known; enables pre-allocation in toArray() and collect()
- **SUBSIZED** (0x4000) – splits also have known sizes; ArrayList reports this, enabling balanced parallel splits
- **NONNULL** (0x100) – no null elements; ConcurrentHashMap reports this
- **IMMUTABLE** (0x400) – source cannot be modified; List.of() collections report this
- **CONCURRENT** (0x1000) – source supports concurrent modification safely; ConcurrentHashMap reports this
s1_definition.analogy: At National Bank of India, characteristics are like labels on a batch of transaction receipts. ORDERED means "these receipts are in chronological order". SORTED means "these receipts are already sorted by amount". DISTINCT means "no duplicate receipt numbers". SIZED means "we know there are exactly 1000 receipts". When the processing pipeline sees SORTED, it skips the sorting step. When it sees SIZED, it pre-allocates exactly 1000 result slots instead of resizing.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Characteristics and Stream Optimizations
  ==========================================

  Collection Characteristics:
  ┌────────────────┬──────────┬───────┬────────┬──────────┐
  │ Collection      │ ORDERED  │ SIZED │ SORTED │ DISTINCT │
  ├────────────────┼──────────┼───────┼────────┼──────────┤
  │ ArrayList       │    Y     │   Y   │   N    │    N     │
  │ HashSet         │    N     │   Y   │   N    │    Y     │
  │ TreeSet         │    Y     │   Y   │   Y    │    Y     │
  │ LinkedHashSet   │    Y     │   Y   │   N    │    Y     │
  └────────────────┴──────────┴───────┴────────┴──────────┘

  Stream Operations vs Characteristics:
  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ Source: TreeSet (ORDERED, SIZED, SORTED, DISTINCT)  │
  │                                                      │
  │ .sorted()   -> SORTED present -> NO-OP              │
  │ .distinct() -> DISTINCT present -> NO-OP            │
  │ .count()    -> SIZED present -> O(1)                │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ Source: ArrayList (ORDERED, SIZED)                   │
  │                                                      │
  │ .filter()   -> SIZED REMOVED                        │
  │ .sorted()   -> SORTED ADDED                         │
  │ .distinct() -> DISTINCT ADDED                       │
  │ .count()    -> SIZED gone -> O(n) must count        │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Spliterator characteristics are metadata flags that the stream pipeline uses to optimise execution. SIZED enables pre-allocation and O(1) counting. SORTED means sorted() is a no-op. DISTINCT means distinct() is a no-op. ORDERED means the stream must maintain encounter order, which can slow down parallel execution. Understanding these flags explains why certain stream operations are free or expensive depending on the source collection.

Different collections report different characteristics. ArrayList is ORDERED and SIZED. HashSet is DISTINCT and SIZED. TreeSet is all four: ORDERED, SIZED, SORTED, and DISTINCT. Stream operations themselves modify characteristics: filter() removes SIZED (count becomes unknown), sorted() adds SORTED, and distinct() adds DISTINCT.

At National Bank of India, Pankaj optimised the end-of-day reporting pipeline by choosing the right source collection for each stream. Account balances stored in a TreeSet could skip sorting and deduplication. Transaction counts stored in an ArrayList could leverage SIZED for pre-allocated arrays. This understanding of characteristics turned stream operations from potentially O(n log n) to O(n) or even O(1).

Remember one sentence: Spliterator characteristics like SIZED, SORTED, and DISTINCT tell the stream pipeline which operations it can skip, making the choice of source collection a performance decision.
